To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the prevalence of end digit preference in blood-pressure measurements in a hypertensive clinic in Nigeria was high, and that nurses had a higher preference for end digit 0 than physicians.
“Nurses and physicians displayed a very high frequency of preference of end digit zero for systolic and diastolic BP readings, and this was more common among nurses than among physicians”.
the high prevalence of end digit preference for zero argues for training, retraining, and certification of healthcare workers in blood pressure (BP).
